name: Chau Doc food guide
summary: Châu Đốc eats fish. Breakfast is bún cá with điên điển at Chợ Châu Đốc, seasoned with chili and lime. Mắm, pickled with palm sugar, salt, chili, and garlic, is stacked in the hall. Dinner is lẩu mắm, the shared pot, and cá kho tộ, a Mekong claypot eaten with rice and greens. Afternoon sweets are bánh bò thốt nốt, bánh bò Chăm in the villages, and chè thốt nốt. Only the claypot has a licensed photograph of the bowl. No stall price was published.
body: The market is the morning. The pot is the evening. Can Tho’s bánh xèo is a different delta breakfast. Do not rename bún cá as that crepe.
specialtiesLead: The card is the dish with a photograph. The other bowls are named above and have no licensed picture, so they are not cards.

sections.heading: Chau Doc Market
paragraphs: Come in the morning. A closing hour was not printed.

sections.heading: Can Tho, if that breakfast is the point
paragraphs: Bánh xèo is the neighbor’s crepe, not the Châu Đốc bowl.
